newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Kras says '96 net profit rises 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Kras says '96 net profit rises 25 pct.

text.p: Leading Croatian chocolate maker Kras said on Wednesday its 1996 net profit rose 25 percent to 18.6 million kuna from 14.8 million.

The company's turnover rose to 670 million from 654 million the previous year. It managed to increase production 2.9 percent and sales 2.5 percent, the company said in a paid advertisment in daily Vecernji List.

Some 29 percent of total sales were exports, which grew eight percent to reach 33 million German marks, Kras said. It sells chocolate in countries including the United States, Saudi Arabia and Russia.
Despite tough international competition the company's share of the Croatian market rose to 40.5 percent from 38.3 percent in 1995.
It launched 30 new products last year, including a new chocolate line Dorina.
Kras said the growth trend had continued into 1997 with profits in the first three months rising 28 percent in comparison with the same period of last year.
But it said government regulations would hit profitability as they forced confectioners to buy domestic sugar, which is up to 50 percent more expensive than imported sugar.

Kras is planning to invest 51 million marks by the end of 1998 in marketing, developing new products and modernising its production line, which should increase the company's overall productivity and profitability.
Its annual production should rise to more than 31,000 tonnes in 2005 from 21,000 tonnes in 1996, it said.
